Output: audit opening/history assessment, corrected coverage and concise result/progress. 2. History-and-uncertainty — Complete MC06, MC08–MC12, MC14 and MC18 using the relevant manuscript passages, normative contracts, fixtures and actual P03–P06 records/code. Distinguish witnesses from complete families, exact from approximate grouping, admissible measures from unsupported probabilities, and default from unsupported or numerical failure. Output each subsection directly to the audit and affected coverage rows before further inspection. Stop when every assigned assessment has exact support, a consequence and a specific remaining obligation; unavailable authority limits the affected claim without stopping independent work.

3. Accounting-and-sectors — Complete MC13, MC15–MC17 and MC19–MC22 against corporate, consolidation/FX, instrument, bank and insurer manuscript cases and actual P08 preparation. Check event-to-treatment-to-journal-to-statement boundaries and the scope of retained calculations. Resolve G4/G7 obligations and relevant G5/G12/G16 intersections. Identify dated authority, elections, transitions, source applicability, unsupported operations, extension constraints and matched-event examples P17 must supply. Preserve P08’s failed/incomplete scope; do not repair historical product modules. Output saved accounting/sector sections and coverage updates. Stop when every domain has an evidence-backed present assessment and concrete P17 obligations, without presenting balanced journals as accounting validity.

4. Language-research-integration — Complete MC23–MC24, MC26–MC33 and MC34–MC35 using actual language/IR contracts, solver boundaries, review interfaces, research/software records and P11/P12 evidence. Carry forward MC01–MC05, MC07 and MC25 without repeating their completed analyses. Replace remaining generic G2/G5/G8/G9/G10 obligations and reconcile all G1–G18 cross-references. Inspect relevant manuscript/PDF passages for MC28/MC32 while preserving the distinction between source inspection, rendered presentation and human comprehension; do not rebuild the manuscript. Assess technical source support and actual reuse capability, not ledger or test counts. Keep feasible internal preparation ahead of any proposed professional question. Output audit sections and coverage rows. Stop when every requirement/gap is specifically assessed and unresolved research, software, document and acceptance work is assigned.

5. Profile-comparison — Compare corporate/shared-IR, typed-library-first, instrument-first and broad sector-first on identical source coverage, joint histories, accounting operations, statements, uncertainty, chronology, review/recovery, extension obligations, authority dependencies and acceptance fixtures. Separate authoring-interface choices from domain scope so alternatives can be combined where appropriate. State tradeoffs, deferred obligations, disqualifying omissions and evidence needed for selection; avoid unsupported effort or superiority rankings. Update the audit, profile fields and open_decisions, including proposed answers, alternatives, consequences and P16 next steps. Stop when all four options receive comparable treatment and every material choice remains explicit.

6. Integrate-review — Reconcile the accumulating audit, coverage and result against all four P15 criteria. Confirm exactly one assessment for every MC01–MC35/G1–G18 and every historical phase, with no generic residual replacing a substantive obligation. Check current reference hashes/anchors and assessment consistency; use registered historical resolutions without recursively revalidating archived reports against mutable inputs. Run the registered P15 checker after final edits; use fresh task-local output if needed, never an existing result file. Update progress within 600 words and result with actual checks, changed files, decision, uncertainty and next action. Return IMPLEMENTED only when the complete audit is supplied and checks pass; the supervisor must still obtain full independent result review. Failed checks or substantive rejection require a revised repair plan.
